meta_chirho.tagline_chirho: A production-grade Haskell compiler implemented in Rust

goals_chirho: Build a production-grade Haskell compiler in Rust approaching 1:1 source compatibility with GHC
Support three execution modes: batch compilation, script execution, interactive REPL
Target LLVM IR for native codegen and WebAssembly as a first-class backend
Compile real Hackage packages, not just toy examples
Improve on GHC internal modularity, diagnostics, portability, and maintainability
Split the implementation into focused Rust crates for fast iteration and portability
Seamless Rust interop: easy to call Haskell from Rust and Rust from Haskell
Portable wherever Rust compiles: the compiler itself should be easy to build and run on any Rust-supported platform
Compile more optimized code via LLVM than GHC where possible
Fault-tolerant architecture: changes in one subsystem should not silently break others; breakage should be caught at compile time via typed phase boundaries
Well-documented codebase structured for AI-assisted development (Claude Code, Codex, etc.)
Compile all Cabal/Hackage libraries as the long-term target

Support compilation profiles: nostd-chirho (minimal runtime, no GC, for demoscene/4k intros), lean-chirho (small runtime), full-chirho (complete runtime with concurrency), compat-chirho (bug-for-bug GHC behavior)
non_goals_chirho: Immediate support for every GHC extension
Peak native-code performance before correctness and compatibility are solid
Locking the project into LLVM-only codegen
Competing with GHC on compile speed in early milestones

compilation_profiles_chirho.description_chirho: Feature-flag-driven compilation profiles that control runtime size, compatibility, and optimization. Selectable via CLI flags or Cabal-level configuration.

profiles_chirho.description_chirho: Minimal or no runtime. No GC, no laziness overhead, no Prelude. For demoscene 4k intros, embedded systems, or bare-metal targets. Haskell as a better C with algebraic types.
Small runtime with basic laziness and simple GC. No concurrency, no profiling. For scripts and small tools.
Complete runtime with concurrency, profiling, full GC. Default for production applications.
Bug-for-bug GHC compatibility mode. Preserves quirky behaviors that real packages depend on. Activated via --compat-profile ghc-9.x flags.
features_chirho: GHC runtime semantics where they diverge

compilation_profiles_chirho.mechanism_chirho: Rust feature flags in rhasky-runtime-chirho and rhasky-driver-chirho. CLI: rhasky build --profile nostd-chirho. Cabal-level: rhasky-profile: nostd-chirho in .cabal files.

success_criteria_chirho: Parse, resolve, and typecheck non-trivial Haskell modules
Compile a curated compatibility suite of real Hackage libraries
Execute scripts with acceptable startup latency
Run an interactive REPL on the same runtime foundations
Emit both LLVM IR and WebAssembly artifacts from the same core pipeline

architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: Memory safety without GC, strong type system, excellent LLVM/Wasm ecosystem support

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Typed phase boundaries with explicit IR transformations
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: Prevents phase confusion, enables independent testing of each pass

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Typed core IR followed by STG-like runtime-oriented IR
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: Proven by GHC, Eta, and UHC. Core handles typed optimization, STG handles closure conversion and laziness
Required by REPL, IDE integration, and formatting tools. Proven by Roslyn and rust-analyzer

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Lexer-level virtual token insertion (virtual braces and semicolons)
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: Haskell Report specifies layout as a lexer transformation. Keeps parser grammar context-free

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Backend-agnostic pipeline; LLVM IR first, WebAssembly first-class; Cranelift, JVM, BEAM as additional targets
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: LLVM provides mature optimization and codegen. Wasm enables browser REPL, sandboxed execution, portability. Cranelift enables fast debug builds. JVM and BEAM enable polyglot interop.

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: 19 focused crates; some start as modules within parent crates and split when they grow
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: Fine-grained crates enable parallel compilation and clear ownership. Starting some as modules avoids premature API stabilization

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Copying generational GC for native; linear-memory GC for Wasm. GC interface abstracted behind a trait
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: Copying GC proven for lazy languages. Wasm GC proposal still evolving so linear-memory is more portable. Trait abstraction lets backends diverge

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Ship minimal rhasky-base-chirho reimplementing core Prelude and primitives, expand incrementally
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: GHC base uses GHC-specific primops impractical to replicate. Clean reimplementation gives full control

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Custom binary format for serialized module signatures; not GHC .hi compatible
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: GHC .hi is tightly coupled to GHC internals. Custom format designed for Rhasky type representation and incremental compilation

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Standard ccall/capi for LLVM path; WASI imports for Wasm path. FFI declarations parsed uniformly
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: ccall is standard Haskell FFI. WASI provides closest Wasm equivalent. Parsing is backend-independent

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Deferred to M8+, but architecture must not preclude it
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: TH requires executing Haskell at compile time. Many popular packages depend on it. Crate graph must allow runtime to be used by driver

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Deferred to M8, but runtime data structures designed thread-safe from the start
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: GHC green thread scheduler is complex. Retrofitting concurrency is a rewrite, so thunk atomicity and heap safety designed in early

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Evaluate for narrow use cases; do not force into the design
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: May help with constraint propagation but a purpose-built solver is likely clearer for type inference

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Structured diagnostics with byte-offset spans, error codes, labeled secondary spans, fix suggestions
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: Good diagnostics are a stated quality goal. Structured errors enable CLI, IDE, and REPL rendering from same data

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Source-compatible with shims where needed; not bug-for-bug
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: Preserve compatibility by default, improve architecture internally. Deviations explicit, testable, documented

architecture_decisions_chirho.decision_chirho: Cabal file parsing in M1, local package databases in M2, Hackage retrieval in M5
architecture_decisions_chirho.rationale_chirho: Testing against real code requires package loading earlier than original M5 placement

evaluation_model_chirho.strategy_chirho: eval/apply with lazy thunks via STG machine (MachineChirho)
evaluation_model_chirho.thunk_chirho: Header word (tag + GC info) + payload. Tag bit distinguishes thunks from values. Blackholing for deadlock detection.

memory_management_chirho.native_chirho: Mark-sweep GC implemented (GcStateChirho); copying generational GC planned. Two-space nursery, aging promotion. Start simple, add generations incrementally.
memory_management_chirho.wasm_chirho: Linear-memory GC. Same algorithm, different memory layout. More portable than Wasm GC proposal.
memory_management_chirho.abstraction_chirho: GC ops behind a trait so backends diverge without changing STG lowering

concurrency_chirho.native_chirho: Green threads on OS threads with work-stealing
concurrency_chirho.early_requirement_chirho: Atomic thunk updates, safe-for-concurrent-GC heap layout from M0

exception_model_chirho.synchronous_chirho: Through IO monad evaluation. try/catch/throw as runtime primitives. Forced thunks can throw.
exception_model_chirho.asynchronous_chirho: Deferred to M8. throwTo semantics requires interruptible ops and masking.
exception_model_chirho.script_chirho: Top-level handler prints exception and exits non-zero

prior_art_chirho.lesson_chirho: Runtime performance on non-native platforms is hard. Focus correctness first. Reusing GHC frontend is viable but creates tight coupling.
Whole-program optimization yields great code but doesn't compose with separate compilation. Use per-module optimization with limited cross-module inlining.
Multi-backend modularity is achievable. Ecosystem adoption requires package compatibility, not just language compatibility.
Diverging from Haskell semantics gains simplicity but loses the ecosystem. Preserve semantics even when inconvenient.
Interpreter-first gives excellent REPL but limits performance ceiling. Support interpretation for scripting while keeping compilation primary.
Alternative GC (region inference) can work but requires deep commitment. Start with proven copying GC.
Red-green trees and salsa-style incremental computation are proven for IDE-quality tooling. Adopt similar patterns.

open_questions_chirho.question_chirho: Should the interpreter share the exact same STG representation as compiled backends?
open_questions_chirho.thinking_chirho: Start with interpreting STG directly. Consider bytecode only if performance or complexity demands it.

open_questions_chirho.question_chirho: What granularity for interface file invalidation?
open_questions_chirho.thinking_chirho: Start per-module hashing, refine to per-declaration fingerprinting if build times warrant.

open_questions_chirho.question_chirho: Should rhasky-base-chirho support rewrite rules from the start?
open_questions_chirho.thinking_chirho: Yes, in the simplifier (M3). Rewrite rules are heavily used in base for list fusion and are critical for performance of idiomatic Haskell.

open_questions_chirho.question_chirho: When should cross-compilation be designed in?
open_questions_chirho.thinking_chirho: Backend-agnostic pipeline supports it conceptually. Explicit cross-compilation deferred to M5+ without architectural risk.
No. GHC .hi format is unstable and deeply coupled to GHC internals. Only Rhasky-compiled packages for the foreseeable future.

open_questions_chirho.question_chirho: Should Cranelift replace LLVM as the primary native backend?
open_questions_chirho.thinking_chirho: Cranelift is faster to compile against and has no LLVM dependency, making it attractive for CI and distribution. However LLVM has more mature optimization passes. Current plan: LLVM for release builds, Cranelift as a fast debug/dev backend. Revisit at M4 with benchmark data.

open_questions_chirho.question_chirho: What is the right target Haskell language version for compatibility?
open_questions_chirho.thinking_chirho: GHC 9.6 / Haskell 2010 plus common extensions as the baseline. GHC 9.8+ features tracked but not blocking M1-M3.
